root_cause_label: Terminal Flooding via Mismanaged Background Monitor Process Due to Missing tmux -t Target Flag
one_sentence_failure_summary: At step 2 the agent issued tmux send-keys without a -t target specifier, causing monitor.py to execute in the host shell rather than inside a tmux pane, flooding the terminal with periodic monitor output for the remaining 73 steps and preventing any command output from being read, while the agent looped on empty-wait steps and ultimately made an unfounded task-complete claim.
t_err_evidence: tmux split-window -h -t workflow creates wrong horizontal split layout instead of required vertical top/bottom split
t_commit_evidence: Once monitor.py starts running in the agent's own shell process group at step 2, it cannot be killed by tmux kill-session or pkill (as confirmed by failed attempts in steps 10, 14, 17, 23, 31), and every subsequent command's output is drowned out by monitor flood lines; the failure is locked in from the moment of the wrong send-keys invocation.
t_surface_evidence: tmux attach-session output shows interleaved monitor output with no proper pane layout visible, confirming incorrect setup
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked knowledge that tmux send-keys without a -t target sends keystrokes to the currently active pane of the calling shell context rather than to the tmux session's pane 0; this caused monitor.py to run in the host shell instead of the intended tmux pane.
